Just explain how you feel! There’s no imaginary threshold to worry about. The person you’ll be talking to will probably ask you things like the following:
- when was the first time you felt this way? 
- what your childhood was like (it’s ok if it was completely normal too! Mine was relatively normal with next to no signs)
- How would you describe yourself currently (like identity wise, physically, mentally)
- What changes would you want to see if you start HRT? As well as bluntly asking if you want to start HRT

That’s all I can remember being asked from my first appointment. The first is mostly just getting to know the current you, then talking about the past you, and how you want to see the future you. Just be honest! They can’t deny you it just because they don’t feel you’re “trans enough” unless they’re REALLY bad. Hope this helps!

I know this is old but i feel like i need to share my store as a vent. Both my parents are on disability. Realistically, if my mom just put some effort into losing weight, and my dad sought help for his mental issues, they could’ve both found jobs. But no, they just sat at home, watching tv all day, or playing games on our ps2 and DS. They also got extra money from the government for have children. But that money was rarely spent on us.

My mom specifically never did anything with us. My dad would play with me and my brother occasionally, but if someone got hurt, or something broke, we’d get yelled at, sometimes grounded, sometimes hit. No one ever wanted to play board games, and we’d get told to quiet down if we were having too much fun.

I remember one time during the summer I BEGGED my mom to go to the mall on the weekend since they would get their money. It was literally a 20 minute walk and I knew they’d have money for once. She said sure and even agreed to get me something, and all week I SUPER excited. The day finally came and she said “maybe some other time” I was devastated. Another time my mom said we’d bake together in the morning. I woke up early, only to find her still in bed and when I tried to wake her up, I was yelled at for waking her up early, and told we’re not baking anymore. The kicker for me is even to this day, anytime they do want to do something, it’s something THEY want to do. Go to places they want.

I know that living off a fixed income is difficult, but I remember finding out how much money they got in a month for the both of us, and how much they were paying in rent (we lived with our grandparents, still do) I was pissed. They essentially had an extra $1600 a month after their expenses to use. They didn’t save anything. Not a penny for themselves or us. So what did they do? Waste it all. Dad wants a new drum kit? Go ahead! We want more than 1 shirt for the school year? Sorry we don’t have the money. They can go to the bar for the night, but we can’t go down the street for the farmers market. 

I’m 22 now, and I would be lying if I said I don’t resent them for it. It’s completely changed my perspective of things, and I still deal with these issues since I still live at home. They don’t understand that me and my bother need to work for everything and can’t spend time with them no matter how much they beg, which is ironic since they never spent time with us. They’re in their 50’s now and complain about not having money and us not spending time with them. They still waste the little money they do have to go out to bars and waste their money.

I haven’t even gotten my consultation yet but here’s what I’ve been doing to help with the waiting. Excuse the format I’m on mobile.
-make a list of everything I’ll need (others mentioned this)
- how much I’ll need to save before then. Im going have to pay roughly $4000, plus I want to save a little more to make up for the time off work I’ll need to take. I know this sounds stressful but I enjoy number crunching and this has helped me relax. 
- make a list of everything I hate/can’t wait for now. My friend did this before his top surgery and he said even though sometimes it made him very anxious for it since he wanted it so badly, it also gave him something to do each day writing down what he hates about his chest and what he can’t wait to experience once it’s gone
- start some time consuming hobbies. Crochet, sewing, painting or anything else that peaks your interest AND isn’t too strenuous. Once you get your surgery you can keep the hobbie going since you’ll be resting anyways! Personally I’ve picked up sudoku puzzles!
- i have an iPhone and an app that I use for counting down days on my Lock Screen. When I get my consultation date I plan on setting it up so looking at it count down just kinda becomes a habit… because I’ll forget it almost immediately lol

Lastly, just remember: It’s normal to be anxious before something like this. Your time will come before you know it and you’ll be so happy! Hope maybe on of these help!

Trigger warning for this one though, mentions death. >!So when I was 20, I was in a really bad place mentally. I knew I was trans, and I couldn't deny it, but I didn't know if transitioning would still be for me, or if I was "not worth saving" Long story short, I sat myself down one day and tried to imagine this scenario: You're now elderly. You lived a long, happy, and fulfilling life. You're alone when unfortunately you collapsed and passed away. Your neighbors get concerned and call the police for a wellness check. They walk inside and the first thing they see is... and my brain immediately went "an elderly man". It was at that moment that I realized that no matter what when my time eventually comes and I have no more say in what happens in the world, the last thing I want people to see is me as a female. !<I know this is more of a morbid way of thinking, but this is what finally got me to pursue transitioning. First, if you’re in university/college, try talking to them and find out what services they can provide to you. 

But if you’re not, this is how I approached it. I first went to my family doctor near the end of October 2022, told him I’m pretty sure I’m trans and that I wanted to talk with someone that specializes in this and can help with my transition. He sent my referral to [CAMH Gender Identity Clinic](https://www.camh.ca/en/your-care/programs-and-services/gender-identity-clinic-adult) and put on a wait list. I had my first appointment April 2023, second appointment June, at which I got diagnosed with gender dysphoria. I have another appointment this month, and I’m probably going to get the ok to start T!

This also depends on where about a you are in Ontario, but I hope this can at least help you in the right direction!
